newsitem.title: INDIA: India, New Zealand sign tax evasion pact.
newsitem.headline: India, New Zealand sign tax evasion pact.

text.p: India and New Zealand have signed an agreement to prevent third-country investors from evading tax by using New Zealand as a conduit for investments in India, the government said on Friday.

"The protocol will prevent the misuse of the provisions of the existing double taxation avoidance convention by investors of third countries using New Zealand as a conduit for routing the investments to India," it said in a statement.

G.K. Mishra, chairman of India's Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), signed the protocol to an existing convention on double taxation. New Zealand high commissioner in India Nicholas Bridge signed for his country.

"Such investors were able to create artificial profits as a means of soaking up tax-spared foreign tax credits," the statement said. "Artificial losses also created in the process could then be used to offset the tax otherwise payable in New Zealand."
